subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Renaissance painters often worked in collaborative workshops where multiple artists contributed to single works.
• Many paintings attributed to master artists were actually completed primarily by their apprentices or assistants.
• The exact attribution of specific elements in many Renaissance works, such as the background landscape in "The Adoration of the Magi," remains disputed among art historians.
• Dr. Guerline Celestin, Eric Stafford, and Elena Kowalski used computer analysis to examine brushstroke patterns and paint composition in Renaissance paintings.
• They determined there is a 23.4% probability that the master artist painted the landscape in "The Adoration of the Magi," concluding that the brushwork is "more consistent with apprentice techniques."
prompt: The student wants to make a generalization about the kind of study conducted by Celestin, Stafford, and Kowalski. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Based on computer analysis, Celestin, Stafford, and Kowalski claim that an apprentice painted the landscape in "The Adoration of the Magi."
choices.B: Researchers have used computer analysis to address questions of attribution within the field of art history.
choices.C: There is only a 23.4% probability that the master artist painted the landscape in "The Adoration of the Magi"; an apprentice is the more likely creator.
choices.D: It is likely that an apprentice, not the master artist, painted the landscape in "The Adoration of the Magi."

explanation:
Choice B is correct. It generalizes that the study by Celestin, Stafford, and Kowalski used computer analysis to address attribution questions in art history.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because the sentence summarizes the methodology and findings of a particular analysis of a single painting; it doesn't make a generalization about the kind of study conducted.
